findings.subject: compatibility-matrix.completed.v1.json #/rows/0 and component-lock-schema.completed.v1.json #/properties/resolved/items/properties/selectedCompatibility/properties/S-CORE
findings.issue: S-CORE merges core release and core-state writer into one supportedReaders [1,1] window, while initial release 0.1.0 has SemVer major 0. The lock S-CORE is only a release string, so it cannot pin the independently named coreState=1. Component state S-STATE is a different surface and cannot silently stand in for core state. The prose blanket initial-major [1,1] makes the contradiction evaluable, not just a naming concern.
findings.requiredChange: Declare separate core-release compatibility and core-state compatibility within S-CORE, or explicitly choose a versioned core API separate from release numbering. Pin both the release and core-state datum in selectedCompatibility; add supported/unsupported examples that accept the actual 0.1.0/1 writer without equating the numbers.

findings.subject: check_compatibility_design.py version() and satisfies()
findings.issue: The contract promises arbitrary nonnegative decimal version components, but Python int conversion rejects more than 4300 digits under the default Python 3.12 limit. A 4301-digit major plus .0.0 passes the authored JSON schema; version() raises ValueError and satisfies(v,v) returns false. This is well below the 4 MiB metadata cap. Numeric prerelease identifiers have the same defect.
findings.requiredChange: Compare normalized decimal strings by length then lexicographic bytes, or explicitly implement an adequate bounded decimal parser consistent with the metadata cap. Add over-4300-digit major and numeric-prerelease equality/ordering fixtures. Do not silently add an unstated small integer bound.

findings.subject: component-lock-schema.completed.v1.json #/properties/resolutionInputs and distribution-runtime-completion.v1.md section 3
findings.issue: The claimed complete resolution input record omits project/global scope and the scoped request context even though section 3 says scope affects selection and project shadowing/global fallback. The inherited DR111 source also names requested profile, capabilities and pins/holds as resolution inputs. Current fields are installId/indexDigest/platform/hostCoreVersion/request/permissionPolicyDigest; request contains only stableId/version or constraint. Different project/global selection contexts can therefore share the same declared inputs and yield different resolved tuples.
findings.requiredChange: Either explicitly fix unused preview profile/capability/pin-hold inputs by normative constants and document that disposition, or include all remaining resolution-affecting inputs with exact types and canonical ordering, including scope/project-selection context. Add a differing-scope fixture and identical-input determinism check.

findings.subject: compatibility-design-cases.v1.json and check_compatibility_design.py
findings.issue: No candidate comparator, tuple comparator or dependency closure property is exercised. ORDER-5 intentionally returns equal precedence for 1.0.0+a/b but no fixture checks the required full-version/provenance/digest tie-break. The only positive lock is one component, while inherited TC-ACCEPT requires a multi-component closure once DR111 activates locks. Missing dependency, undeclared edge, required-cycle, backtrack from an unsatisfiable highest candidate, scope fallback and duplicate tuple conflict remain absent.
findings.requiredChange: Before treating this package as complete compatibility design evidence, author finite explicit selection/closure fixtures with exact expected selected tuples/refusal, implement a reference comparator/closure model or bind a separately reviewed package that does, and pin that join. This is not a request to implement a shipping solver.

findings.subject: compatibility-matrix.completed.v1.json and check_compatibility_design.py run()
findings.issue: Matrix checking counts rows and active flags only. It does not evaluate both-declared-range intersection, selected pin membership, support-clock edges or security revocation overriding support. The lock structural schema accepts S-CTRL=2 and empty/conflicting closure sets, correctly within structural-only scope, but no paired semantic negative fixture distinguishes those inputs from admitted compatible locks.
findings.requiredChange: Add semantic matrix/pin/support-boundary examples or a reviewed executable join, including 0.1.0 core acceptance after COMP-M1, nonintersection, unsupported selected major, and 90-day/one-subsequent-minor edge cases.

acceptedPoints: Prerelease admission correctly requires an exact match or a same-core prerelease endpoint; build metadata ignored for precedence and distinguished for exact release requests.
Lock includes every inherited top-level and tuple field, adds public policy digest, rejects unknown fields, and explicitly distinguishes structural validity from trust/closure.

Security canonical-profile dependency is openly conditional. Its unspecified identity is an integration dependency, not standalone evidence of an admitted lock; acceptance of final integrated lock requires exact accepted profile and byte goldens.
